name: Treaty of Meersen
summary: On the death of Lothair II without legitimate heirs, his uncles Louis the German and Charles the Bald divide his Middle-Frankish realm (Lotharingia) between them. The line runs from the North Sea down the Meuse to the Saône, establishing the linguistic Romance/Germanic boundary in the Low Countries that survives to the modern Belgian language divide.

_quarry.structural_significance: Eliminates the imperial 'Middle Kingdom' as a separate political unit; the contested Lotharingian space becomes the persistent fault line of West European politics through the modern era.
